assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: wide A5 field-guide section illustration, intended to print about 116 mm wide and no more than 52 mm high
Input images: Image 1 is the governing style reference only. Image 2 is a selected illustration from the same handbook and is also a style reference only. Preserve their meticulous black-ink engraving craft, fine stippling and cross-hatching, technical realism, line weight, contrast, and pure-white paper. Do not copy either reference's machine, objects, or composition.
Primary request: Create an original, unlabeled natural-history engraving for 'the Amanita warning constellation.' Show one deliberately generic Amanita-form mushroom specimen excavated intact and angled in a graceful three-quarter botanical-study pose. The cap is slightly tipped so pale free gills are clearly visible underneath; the stem carries a delicate, plausibly fragile ring; the complete base is visible with a rounded bulb emerging from a torn saclike volva and a few loose crumbs of soil. The image must communicate a warning pattern for stopping and seeking expert review, not a species portrait or an edibility verdict.
Scene/backdrop: pure opaque white paper, no horizon and no environment
Subject: one complete generic Amanita-form specimen only; no humans, no equipment
Style/medium: meticulous nineteenth-century scientific natural-history engraving in black ink, fine stippling and cross-hatching, consistent in craft and contrast with both reference images
Composition/framing: very wide horizontal composition around 2.2:1; specimen centered and fully visible; cap, gills, entire stem, ring, bulb, and volva all inside the frame; calm editorial scale; generous crop-safe white margins on every side; no element cut off
Color palette: black ink only on pure white
Constraints: illustration only; no text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, leader lines, arrows, icons, logos, border, frame, watermark, color, gray paper, transparency, cast shadow, or decorative background; morphologically plausible but deliberately not identifiable to a particular species; do not imply that these features prove toxicity or edibility
Avoid: vector schematic, infographic, labeled anatomy plate, callout boxes, flowchart, cartoon, generic clip art, photorealistic photograph, decorative botanical scene, multiple mushroom species, basket, food, kitchen, skull, hazard symbol, gore, dramatic horror
assets.selectionRationale: The single fully excavated specimen makes the gills, fragile ring, bulb, and saclike volva visible without labels or a taxonomic key. Its wide natural-history engraving treatment matches the handbook while the adjacent prose retains the safety limits.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: wide A5 field-guide comparison illustration, intended to print about 116 mm wide and about 45-50 mm high
Input images: Image 1 is the governing style reference only. Image 2 is a selected illustration from the same handbook and is also a style reference only. Preserve their meticulous black-ink engraving craft, fine stippling and cross-hatching, technical natural-history realism, line weight, contrast, and pure-white paper. Do not copy either reference's machine, mushroom specimen, or composition.
Primary request: Create one original, unlabeled paired botanical comparison plate supporting a handbook warning about true morels versus false-morel look-alikes. The illustration must communicate a structural comparison for stopping and seeking expert review, never an edibility certification.
Scene/backdrop: pure opaque white paper, no horizon and no environment
Subject: two clearly separated specimen groups with equal visual weight. LEFT GROUP: one generic true-morel-form specimen with a conical cap whose surface has unmistakable deep hole-like pits bounded by raised ridges, plus a clean longitudinal half-section beside it showing one continuous open hollow cavity through cap and stalk. RIGHT GROUP: one generic Gyromitra-like false-morel-form specimen with an irregular lobed, folded, brainlike cap, plus a clean longitudinal half-section beside it showing irregular internal chambers and folded or solid-looking tissue rather than one continuous hollow cavity. Keep both groups morphologically plausible but deliberately generic, not portraits of named species.
Style/medium: meticulous nineteenth-century scientific natural-history engraving in black ink, fine stippling and cross-hatching, consistent in craft and contrast with both reference images
Composition/framing: very wide horizontal composition around 2.2:1; left group occupies the left half and right group the right half with a generous blank center gutter; all whole specimens and longitudinal sections fully visible; calm editorial scale; generous crop-safe white margins on every side; no element cut off; no ground line or cast shadow
Color palette: black ink only on pure white
Constraints: illustration only; no text, letters, numbers, labels, captions, leader lines, arrows, brackets, icons, logos, border, frame, watermark, color, gray paper, transparency, cast shadow, decorative background, people, tools, basket, food, or kitchen; the left form must visibly read as pitted rather than merely wrinkled; the right form must visibly read as lobed/brainlike rather than pitted; the cut sections must not be swapped; do not imply that appearance alone proves toxicity or edibility
Avoid: vector schematic, infographic, diagram boxes, callout marks, cartoon, generic clip art, photorealistic photograph, decorative botanical scene, hazard symbol, skull, gore, dramatic horror
assets.refinementPrompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: targeted correction to an A5 field-guide comparison illustration
Input images: Image 1 is the edit target. Images 2 and 3 are style references only.
Primary request: Change only the longitudinal cut section of the true-morel form, which is the second specimen from the left. Make its single continuous interior cavity unmistakably empty and hollow: pure white paper inside the cavity, bounded by a thin engraved inner wall from cap through stalk, with no stippling, gray fill, tissue, septa, or chambers inside that cavity.
Constraints: Preserve the positions, proportions, exterior morphology, pitted true-morel whole specimen, lobed false-morel whole specimen, false-morel cut section and its irregular filled/chambered interior, black-ink natural-history engraving style, pure white background, wide composition, margins, and all other details exactly. No text, labels, arrows, border, color, or watermark. Do not redesign any specimen.
assets.selectionRationale: The paired whole and longitudinal-section studies make the pitted continuous-hollow pattern visibly distinct from the irregular brainlike non-hollow warning pattern without embedding labels or presenting the image as an edibility key. A targeted refinement removed ambiguous shading from the true-morel cavity; the adjacent editable prose retains the poison warning and safety limit.
